description: F.1 — Test the leading-order derived E_0 formula at 50 dps: E_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)). With this E_0 and the symbolic NF difference Δ(net) = h(h-2)/2 (h = q - q^-1), predict free-neutron Q_β and compare to CODATA. Validates calibration-inputs.md claim that the leading-order formula is 0.17% off (1.3 keV residual on Q_β); the gap is the brane-tower correction that requires F.2.
interpretation: The leading-order formula E_0 = m_e/(q(q-1)) gives Q_β to +0.168%, matching calibration-inputs.md's stated +0.17% leading-order error. The +1.3 keV residual is the next-order brane-tower correction. To collapse 3 calibrations -> 2, we need F.2 to derive this 1.3 keV correction algebraically (no further calibration). Several alternate functional forms tried; m_e/(q(q-1)) is by far the closest at leading order — others miss by 30-1100%, ruling them out as candidate closed forms.
next_steps: F.2: derive the 1.3 keV tower correction algebraically; expected to come from the brane-tower n=1 contribution at H_3(q) — see prop:mass-endomorphism-tower for the tower expansion.
If F.2 closes Qb residual to ppb, the third calibration input (Q_β) becomes derived from (q_0, m_e); 3 cal -> 2 cal.
